title: Roblox Shares Fall 3.8% on Google and Unity AI Gaming Launch

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Unity has introduced Spark, a tool that enables creators to develop 3D and professional-level video games through conversational AI prompts without writing code. Users can start from templates or scratch to modify game physics, characters, and rules via a chat interface, with some game genres supporting multiplayer modes and leaderboards. This functionality complements Google's Playground experiment, which is currently available to US users aged 18 and older, though only subscribers on paid plans can generate new games.

Shares of Roblox fell 3.8% in pre-market trading, while Unity rose 5% following the announcement of the partnership. The collaboration allows AI-generated games to be distributed through Google Play, providing Unity with a wide distribution layer to challenge creator platforms like Roblox and AppLovin. The technology is powered by Google's Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria AI models.

selectedTweets.text:
Google released Playground, an experimental AI gaming platform that lets people build playable games from text prompts without writing code.

Creators can start from scratch or templates, then change game physics, rules, characters, and environments through conversation. 

Games run in the browser, can be kept private or shared publicly, and some genres support multiplayer and leaderboards. 

Google is also planning an integration with Unity Spark for more advanced 3D and professional-level game creation.
